newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares slip 2.2 pct as small investors flee.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares slip 2.2 pct as small investors flee.

text.p: Egyptian shares fell an average of 2.2 percent on Monday as small investors again tried to pull out of the market in panic at slumping prices, brokers said.
But the average transaction size increased from Sunday's level in what brokers said was a sign that some institutions were cautiously stepping in to take advantage of low prices.
"It's approaching the lowest point, the point at which a recovery will happen," said Ahmed al-Helw of Intercapital.

The Capital Market Authority's all-share index dropped 8.26 points to 364.79, the lowest level since January 29. The index has now shed 14.7 percent since it hit an all-time high of 427.77 points on February 24, exactly one month ago.
Volume was 114.5 million pounds ($33.7 million), almost half of it from a partial privatisation of Cairo Housing and Development, which was oversubscribed 65 percent.
The state had offered 1.272 million shares in Cairo Housing but decided to meet all the demand. It sold 2.080 million shares, all at the minimum price of 24.72 pounds a share.
Helw said the demand for the shares was higher than expected and now that the state had relinquished majority control of the company investors could expect performance to improve.
But the stock slipped in post-privatisation trading, ending the day at 24.50, 0.22 off the striking price.
The sell-off hit all the dominant sectors, banks, millers, and cements, with only a handful of individual exceptions.
After Cairo Housing, the most active share was Central and West Delta Flour Mills, which fell 4.00 to 92.25 in trade worth 4.16 million pounds.
Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA bucked the downward trend, rising 1.00 to 78.00 pounds, while Amriyah Cement held its ground at 81.00 in relatively thin trade.

The more diverse finance sector was more mixed. Blue chip Commercial International Bank fell again, by 4.19 to 79.73, despite announcing an 11 percent rise in 1996 results on Sunday. ING Barings in London said the results were almost exactly in line with its and the market's expectations.
"CIB is a stock that's in the hands of small investors for the moment and they want to get out," said Helw.
The index for openly traded firms fell sharply, to 558.2 from 578.74 on Sunday, and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms slipped to 253.96 from 257.58.
Out of the 90 shares traded, 15 gained, 45 lost and 30 ended the day unchanged.
